request.statement:
The submission MUST define `mediate_permissions(frames, permissions, sensitive, force_location, initial_handlers, events)` and MUST return `(callbacks, suppressed, unlocks)` without performing I/O.

`frames` is a sequence of `(frame_id, parent_id, process_id, isolated)` records. IDs are unique integers, each `parent_id` is `None` or another frame ID, and the records form a rooted forest. `permissions` contains distinct strings, `sensitive` is a subset of it, `force_location` is Boolean, and `initial_handlers` lists permissions whose handlers initially exist.

Events are indexed from zero and are `("REQUEST", batch_id, frame_id, requested, deadline)`, `("RESPOND", batch_id, index, decision)`, `("REMOVE", permission)`, `("INSTALL", permission)`, or `("DESTROY", frame_id)`. Batch IDs are unique. `requested` is nonempty, its positions are zero-based, and `decision` is `"ALLOW"` or `"DENY"`. A request at event index `i` satisfies `i < deadline <= len(events)`. Responses may be late, duplicated, or reference nonexistent batches or positions. All other referenced IDs and permissions are valid. There are at most 200,000 frames and events, and at most 300,000 requested positions.

At each index, before processing that event, every pending batch whose deadline equals that index MUST fix all its still-awaiting positions to `"DENY"`. Any resulting callbacks occur in ascending batch-ID order before effects of the indexed event. Deadline `len(events)` is processed after the final event and uses that index in the output.

A request for a dead frame is suppressed immediately. Otherwise, an isolated frame immediately receives `"DENY"` at every position. For any other frame, forced location denial takes precedence: if `force_location` is true and the permission is `"location"`, that position immediately becomes `"DENY"`. Each remaining position awaits a response if its permission currently has an installed handler; otherwise it immediately becomes `"DENY"`.

A response affects only the stated position while it is awaiting a response in a pending batch. An accepted response fixes its decision. The first accepted `"ALLOW"` ever observed for each `(process_id, permission)` pair permanently unlocks that capability if the permission is sensitive.

`REMOVE` atomically uninstalls its handler and fixes every position currently awaiting that permission to `"DENY"`. Removing an absent handler has no additional effect. Resulting callbacks use ascending batch ID. `INSTALL` affects only later requests and is idempotent.

`DESTROY` marks every live frame in the specified static subtree dead. Pending batches belonging to those frames are canceled, produce no callback, and ignore later responses and deadlines. Suppressions caused by one destruction use ascending batch ID. Existing callbacks and unlocks remain unchanged.

A batch produces exactly one callback as soon as all positions are fixed. `callbacks` contains `(event_index, batch_id, result_tuple)` in occurrence order. `suppressed` contains `(event_index, batch_id)` in occurrence order. `unlocks` contains `(event_index, process_id, permission)` in occurrence order.
